key_insight: Positional disorder in realistic resonant dipole-dipole interacting networks can strongly localize excitations, even though the coupling is partially long-ranged and dissipative.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a design route for more robust energy-trapping and transport-control elements in coherent photovoltaics, excitonic circuits, quantum memory, and quantum sensing.
method: Model disordered spin/atom networks with realistic resonant dipole-dipole interaction (RDDI).
Analyze the competition between coherent exchange and dissipative radiative coupling.
Identify localization behavior and a wavelength-driven transition between extended and localized dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical analysis showing that positional disorder in RDDI networks induces strong spatial localization and a photon-wavelength-controlled transition in excitation dynamics.
watch_item: Because the effect relies on realistic open-system RDDI and positional disorder, implementation may be sensitive to geometry, wavelength, and radiative losses in experimental platforms.
paper_title: Quantum state localization in dipole-dipole interacting disordered networks
